_comment: Anchors excluded from a CVE's compiled template family.
Stage 2 offers each resource label as a ladder of rungs, the widest fixing a
single path component -- the area a product serves. That rung earns its place
when a capture recorded a different resource of the same vulnerable surface
than the PoC named (CVE-2023-40044 aligns only through its */AHT/* rung). But
where the component is an ordinary word, or names a surface the product serves
for unrelated purposes, the rung stops identifying the exploited resource and
matches whatever else is filed beneath it.
Each entry below records one such rung together with what it was observed
matching. Excluding it never removes the CVE's own detection: the narrower
rungs, and the other members of the family, carry that.
A branch is only ever dropped when the label keeps at least one other.

CVE-2023-22515.why: an installer area every web application has; matched an Openfire admin-console traversal (/setup/setup-s/%u002e%u002e/%u002e%u002e/plugin-admin.jsp) and an unrelated Confluence setup endpoint

CVE-2023-29298.why: the whole ColdFusion runtime directory; matched a static script asset (/CFIDE/scripts/ajax/package/cfajax.js) rather than the administrator endpoint the PoC names

CVE-2023-35078.why: the Ivanti EPMM application root; matched a sibling API path under a different space prefix (/mifs/asfV3/api/v2/authorized/users)

CVE-2024-4040.why: the CrushFTP web root; matched the product's login page (/WebInterface/login.html), which every deployment serves

CVE-2024-1708.why: the endpoint of the auth bypass this PoC chains through before its own payload; it identifies that step rather than this CVE, and matched a capture of it
